title: Headache

rationale.Physical Exam: HEENT / Neck: Ipsilateral lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, ptosis.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: No focal deficits. Distinguish from other primary headaches.
rationale.CT/MRI brain: Rule out secondary causes — pituitary lesion, vascular abnormality. Normal in cluster.
rationale.High-flow O2 12-15L/min via non-rebreath: First-line acute. Aborts attack in ~15 min.
rationale.Verapamil: First-line prophylaxis. Start low, titrate. Monitor ECG (AV block).
rationale.Prednisone taper: Bridge therapy for rapid suppression while verapamil takes effect.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with severe unilateral orbital/supraorbital/temporal headache lasting 15-180 minutes, occurring in clusters (multiple times per day for weeks-months then remission). Associated ipsilateral autonomic features: lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, eyelid edema, miosis/ptosis (Horner's). Patient is restless/agitated during attacks (unlike migraine where patient lies still). Triggers: alcohol during cluster period. More common in men. First-line acute treatment: high-flow 100% oxygen 12-15 L/min via non-rebreather (aborts attack within 15 min) AND/OR subcutaneous sumatriptan 6mg. Bridge therapy: verapamil (first-line prophylaxis), prednisone taper for rapid suppression. Avoid triggers during cluster period. Refer to neurology.
